launch-desk.sentence: Tidewell has agreed to buy the messaging app Murmurline.
Tidewell is paying entirely in cash, with no stock in the mix.
The companies expect the deal to close by mid-2027.

byteward.sentence: Tidewell is buying Murmurline, the popular messaging app.
The deal values Murmurline at $3.2 billion.
About 85 million people use Murmurline every month.

bench-and-bill.sentence: Tidewell has agreed to buy Murmurline, the messaging app.
Tidewell already owns Skerry, a messaging app with 140 million users.
Two lawmakers have already asked antitrust regulators to take a close look at the deal.
If regulators block it, Tidewell owes Murmurline a $250 million breakup fee.
Tidewell has also promised to keep Murmurline's end-to-end encryption.

ohm-and-bit.sentence: Tidewell is buying the messaging app Murmurline.
Murmurline encrypts every message end to end, so only the sender and the recipient can read it.
Tidewell says Murmurline will keep that protection.
Tidewell's own messaging app, Skerry, doesn't encrypt messages end to end.
Tidewell wants Murmurline and Skerry users to be able to message each other by 2028.
